title: Inventions & Great Discoveries
description: 36 original questions on groundbreaking inventors, historic technologies, and accidental scientific breakthroughs.
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: Who invented the movable-type printing press in Europe around 1440, sparking the printing revolution?
questions.explanation: Gutenberg's press made books affordable and dramatically accelerated literacy and science.

questions.prompt: Who is credited with patenting the first practical telephone in 1876?
questions.explanation: Bell's famous first spoken words over the wire were to his assistant Thomas Watson.

questions.prompt: Who invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN?
questions.explanation: Berners-Lee created HTTP, HTML, and the first web browser and released them royalty-free.

questions.prompt: Which two brothers achieved the first powered, controlled airplane flight at Kitty Hawk in 1903?
questions.explanation: Their Flyer stayed aloft for 12 seconds and covered 36.5 meters on its first flight.

questions.prompt: Which scientist discovered X-rays in 1895 and won the very first Nobel Prize in Physics?
questions.explanation: Röntgen took the first X-ray photograph of his wife Anna's hand.

questions.prompt: Which pioneer discovered the radioactive elements polonium and radium and won Nobel Prizes in both Physics and Chemistry?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie remains the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.

questions.prompt: Which engineer accidentally invented the microwave oven in 1945 after a radar magnetron melted a candy bar in his pocket?
questions.explanation: Spencer worked at Raytheon and next tested popcorn kernels and an egg.

questions.prompt: Which Swiss engineer invented Velcro in 1941 after noticing burdock burrs sticking to his dog's fur?
questions.explanation: Velcro combines the French words 'velours' (velvet) and 'crochet' (hook).

questions.prompt: Who invented the alternating current (AC) induction motor and polyphase power distribution system?
questions.explanation: Tesla's AC system allowed electricity to be transmitted efficiently over long distances.

questions.prompt: Which Scottish engineer's improvements to the steam engine (separate condenser) powered the Industrial Revolution?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of power — the watt — is named in his honor.

questions.prompt: Who invented dynamite in 1867 and later established the famous international prizes bearing his name?
questions.explanation: Nobel held 355 patents during his lifetime.

questions.prompt: Which 11th-century Arab polymath wrote the 'Book of Optics' (Kitab al-Manazir) and laid foundations for the camera obscura and scientific method?
questions.explanation: Known in Latin as Alhazen, he proved that vision occurs when light enters the eye.

questions.prompt: Which 9th-century scholar's treatise on equations gave us the word 'algebra' and whose Latinized name gave us 'algorithm'?
questions.explanation: Al-Khwarizmi worked at the House of Wisdom in Baghdad.

questions.prompt: Which 19th-century mathematician wrote the first published computer algorithm for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine?
questions.explanation: Lovelace envisioned that computing machines could manipulate symbols beyond pure numbers.

questions.prompt: Which Hollywood actress and inventor co-patented frequency-hopping spread spectrum technology, a precursor to Wi-Fi and Bluetooth?
questions.explanation: She developed the torpedo guidance concept with composer George Antheil in 1941.

questions.prompt: Which French educator invented the raised-dot reading and writing system for blind people in 1824?
questions.explanation: Braille devised his 6-dot tactile cell when he was just 15 years old.

questions.prompt: Which ancient civilization invented paper around 105 AD, traditionally credited to Cai Lun?
questions.explanation: Cai Lun standardized papermaking from mulberry bark, hemp, and rags.

questions.prompt: Which German engineer patented the first modern gasoline-powered automobile (Motorwagen) in 1886?
questions.explanation: His wife Bertha Benz famously completed the world's first long-distance road trip in 1888.

questions.prompt: Who invented the Morse code telegraph system in the 1830s?
questions.explanation: The first official telegraph message in 1844 read 'What hath God wrought'.

questions.prompt: Which Italian physicist and inventor pioneered long-distance radio transmission and won the 1909 Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: Marconi sent the first transatlantic wireless radio signal in 1901.

questions.prompt: Which chemist invented the periodic table of elements in 1869, leaving gaps for undiscovered elements?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev accurately predicted the properties of gallium, scandium, and germanium.

questions.prompt: Which British scientist discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831, making electric generators possible?
questions.explanation: Faraday's discoveries underpin nearly every electric motor and power plant today.

questions.prompt: Which Italian physicist invented the first true electric battery (the voltaic pile) in 1800?
questions.explanation: The unit of electrical potential — the volt — is named after him.

questions.prompt: Which American chemist accidentally created Post-it Notes' low-tack adhesive in 1968 at 3M?
questions.explanation: His colleague Art Fry later used the adhesive to make repositionable hymnal bookmarks.

questions.prompt: Which accidental 1938 discovery by DuPont chemist Roy Plunkett produced non-stick Teflon (PTFE)?
questions.explanation: Plunkett found that pressurized tetrafluoroethylene gas had polymerized into a slippery white wax.

questions.prompt: Who invented vulcanized rubber in 1839, making durable tires possible?
questions.explanation: Goodyear accidentally dropped rubber mixed with sulfur onto a hot stove.

questions.prompt: Which 12th-century mechanical engineer from Mesopotamia designed the elephant clock, crankshaft, and programmable automata?
questions.explanation: Al-Jazari's 1206 'Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices' is a landmark of engineering.

questions.prompt: Which French scientist developed the germ theory of disease and the heat-treatment process of pasteurization?
questions.explanation: Pasteur also developed the first vaccines for rabies and anthrax.

questions.prompt: Which Scottish inventor demonstrated the first working mechanical television system in 1926?
questions.explanation: Baird transmitted the first live moving television image in London in January 1926.

questions.prompt: Which three Bell Labs physicists invented the transistor in 1947, launching the modern electronics era?
questions.explanation: They shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics for the transistor.

questions.prompt: Which American computer scientist pioneered the first compiler and helped design the COBOL language?
questions.explanation: Admiral Grace Hopper popularized machine-independent programming languages.

questions.prompt: Which American inventor developed the phonograph and the first commercially practical incandescent light bulb?
questions.explanation: Edison's Menlo Park lab became the model for modern industrial R&D.

questions.prompt: Which 17th-century Dutch microscopist was the first to observe bacteria and single-celled 'animalcules'?
questions.explanation: Van Leeuwenhoek handcrafted single-lens microscopes capable of magnifying over 200x.

questions.prompt: Which scientist formulated the three laws of motion and universal gravitation in his 1687 'Principia'?
questions.explanation: Newton also co-invented calculus and built the first practical reflecting telescope.

questions.prompt: Which ancient Greek mathematician shouted 'Eureka!' upon discovering the principle of buoyancy?
questions.explanation: Archimedes also designed compound pulleys and the Archimedes' screw water pump.

questions.prompt: Which German inventor created the compression-ignition engine that bears his name in the 1890s?
questions.explanation: Diesel engines achieve higher thermal efficiency than spark-ignition gasoline engines.
